title: Environment Variables
definition: Values that are dynamically injected into the application at runtime or build time, keeping sensitive secrets (like API keys and Database passwords) completely out of the source code.
simpleExplanation: You NEVER type your Database Password directly into `db.ts`. If you commit it to GitHub, hackers will find it and delete your database in 5 minutes. Instead, you put it in a `.env` file, which is explicitly ignored by GitHub.
realWorldExample: Using a `.env.development` file on your laptop to connect to a local dummy database, and using Vercel's dashboard to set the Production environment variables to connect to the real database.

basic: What prefix MUST you add to an environment variable in Next.js if you want it to be exposed to the browser (Client Components)?
intermediate: If a variable is named `DATABASE_URL` (without the prefix), can a Client Component read it?

answers.question: Client read without prefix?
answers.answer: No. Next.js heavily protects standard environment variables. If it doesn't have the prefix, it is completely stripped from the client bundle. It will return `undefined` in the browser.
